walkthrough: Goal: paint a long colour copy the way the app paints, with V大's four brushes from the toolbox, knowing which to take when: one way of painting, no second set of pens beside the brushes (the main session's review of S100: the copy opened on the full interface with a card of practice pens beside it while the brush panel named another brush).

Entry: a blank artwork, the Ink Pen. Tap the Brush button, then Painting: the set opens with V大's four, Hard Paint, Hard Round, Soft Brush and Textured Round, each with the stroke it paints, then Flat and Opaque Paint. Texture holds Speckle.

Hard Paint: tap it (outlined: chosen), tap it again: its editor opens in place, its name, the Set row with Painting in the pill, the preview strip, its settings. Back. A stroke as light as the pen allows and one at full pressure: both the colour picked, solid, never paler; the light one a little narrower (pressure sets only its size). Crossing itself it never darkens.

The long colour copy: Home, Practice options, Import practice pack… (the test pack), New copy…, Medium, the vase. Its How names the four brushes and when: Hard Paint for blocks, the colour picked however lightly I press; Hard Round for transitions, pressed lightly for a thin layer where two colours turn into each other; Soft Brush, the airbrush, only where the picture's own edge or gradient is soft; Textured Round for texture, later; then the order of work: the overall tone over the frame with Hard Paint large, the middle tones by colour, the hierarchy and detail smaller.

Got it: the full interface, as on any artwork: Home, Actions and the rest at the top left, the brushes and the colour at the top right, the side bar. No card of pens beside the frame, no All tools: the copy has no tools of its own. The Brush button opens Painting with Hard Paint outlined; the side bar's size is 256 pixels, as large to the 1,600-pixel frame as Big is to an exercise's.

A colour from the colour panel, a light stroke across the vase: the colour picked, solid, the same stroke S100's hard tip laid. Then Hard Round pressed lightly to heavily, Soft Brush across the top, Textured Round along the bottom: each the toolbox's own brush at its own size. Undo takes the last one back, Redo returns it.

Hard Paint's size moved on the side bar; back home; the app closed and opened again. The copy reopened from the practice options: my strokes as they were, Hard Paint chosen again at 256 pixels (a copy opens at the size for its frame); its How not again (told once); a light stroke at that size.
Afterwards, a new artwork: the toolbox is the app's, not the copy's, so Hard Paint stays chosen, as a brush chosen by hand would (Procreate's model).

Toolboxes kept before 1.18.1 get Hard Paint first in Painting, their arrangement kept (the app's tests); strokes drawn before keep their recipes. In Chinese (this file, s104-hard-paint run as on a Chinese tablet): 硬边颜料, 硬圆笔, 柔边笔, 纹理圆笔 in the panel and the How; the steps and the canvas hashes are s104-hard-paint's.
Not here: the author's hand on the tablet; Compare on the copy (S82's, unchanged).
